Chapter 9: The Ongoing Struggle for Justice
As life grew richer for him, the world seemed to get only more complicated.
Do you ever feel like the issues you cared about as a kid—things like inequality, racism, or just that sense that hope is slipping away—never really go away? He sure did. The older he got, the heavier that responsibility felt, like turning away from the fight for justice just wasn’t an option.
He watched new generations stepping up, taking on the same fights, only in new ways. Old battles, new faces. And honestly, it was easy to get cynical, to wonder if anything ever really changes.
But then there were these flashes of courage—people standing up for what’s right, even when it was tough. Those moments? They kept him believing.
He often thought back to what his mother taught him: that ordinary people truly do have power. And his father—his dreams were both a blessing and a weight to carry. Over time, he realized, justice isn’t about being perfect. It’s about sticking with it, showing up, and pressing on, even when the odds seem stacked against you.
So, he found himself drawn into new ways to serve. He worked with young people, spoke out about issues that mattered. And he saw that fighting for justice isn’t just about changing laws or passing new policies. It’s about changing hearts and minds.
It’s about building real relationships—creating spaces where people can truly talk about what scares them, and what gives them hope.
Of course, there were setbacks. Sometimes, he wondered if anything he did actually mattered. But then, maybe at a protest, or just in a quiet, honest conversation, he’d see that little spark—the reminder that change is possible, and that the struggle is always worth it.
What really hit home for him was this: the work of justice isn’t just about helping other people. It’s about working on yourself, too. It’s about being someone who can face the world’s brokenness without giving up hope. Someone who can see the humanity in everyone, even those who don’t agree with you.
The fight for justice—it’s a lifelong journey. It asks us to be brave, to stay humble, and to keep trying, no matter what.
